indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.2.1.4: Recognize water and air as important natural resources
indicator.objective: Identify sources and uses of water in the home and at school

skills.description: Name sources of water at home, school and community
Match a use to the correct setting or to a source

misconceptions: Rain is not a source of water.
We only use water for drinking.
The sea is good for drinking water.

questions.stem: Where do we usually get water in our homes?
hints: It is in the kitchen or bathroom.
questions.explanation: We usually get water from a tap in our homes.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water only comes from rivers.

questions.stem: What do we use water for?
hints: You need it to stay alive.
questions.explanation: We use water for drinking.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water is only for washing.

questions.stem: Which of these is a source of water?
hints: It is a body of water.
questions.explanation: A river is a source of water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water only comes from taps.

questions.stem: What do we use to wash our hands?
questions.explanation: We use water and soap to wash our hands.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any liquid can be used for washing.

questions.stem: Where do we get rain from?
questions.explanation: Rain falls from clouds in the sky.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think rain comes from the ground.

questions.stem: Ama wants to cook rice. What does she need?
hints: You boil the rice in it.
questions.explanation: Ama needs water to cook rice.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think cooking only needs fire.

questions.stem: Which of these is a source of water in a village?
questions.explanation: A borehole is a source of water in a village.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think boreholes are only in cities.

questions.stem: Where is water used for watering plants?
questions.explanation: Water is used for watering plants in the school garden.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water is only for drinking.

questions.stem: Why do we use water in the school toilet?
hints: It helps keep the toilet clean.
questions.explanation: Water is used to flush the toilet.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think toilets use sand.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a source of water?
hints: Which one does not hold or give water?
questions.explanation: A stone is not a source of water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think stones hold water because they are found in water.

questions.stem: Write one way you use water at school.
hints: What do you do after using the toilet?
What do you do before eating?
questions.explanation: There are many ways to use water at school, such as washing hands or flushing the toilet.
questions.misconception: Pupils may only think of drinking.

questions.stem: Name one source of water in your community.
questions.explanation: A tap, river, well, borehole, or rain are all sources of water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water only comes from shops.

questions.stem: Kofi has a bucket. He wants to get water from the ground. Which source should he go to?
hints: It is dug in the ground.
questions.explanation: A well is a source of water dug in the ground.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know what a well is.

questions.stem: Why is water important for our health?
options: It keeps us hydrated and clean
hints: What happens if you don't drink water?
What do you use to wash?
questions.explanation: Water keeps us hydrated and helps us stay clean, which is important for health.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water is only for fun.

questions.stem: Which of these sources of water is safe to drink without treating it?
options: Rain that has just fallen on the ground
hints: Which one is cleaned by the government?
questions.explanation: Tap water is treated and usually safe to drink. River and stream water may contain dirt and germs.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all natural water is safe to drink.

questions.stem: Write two uses of water at home.

criteria.description: Names one correct use (e.g., drinking, cooking)

hints: What do you do when you are thirsty?
What do you do before cooking?
questions.explanation: We use water for drinking and cooking.

questions.stem: Why would a farmer need water on a farm?
questions.explanation: A farmer needs water to water the crops so they can grow.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think farms only need rain.

questions.stem: Which of these is a natural source of water?
hints: It is not made by people.
questions.explanation: Rain is a natural source of water. Taps and bottled water are man-made.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all water sources are man-made.

questions.stem: Tell me one way you use water at home and one way you use it at school.
hints: What do you do in the bathroom?
What do you do in the school toilet?
questions.explanation: Water is used for many things at home and school, like drinking, cooking, washing, and flushing.

questions.stem: Write the name of one source of water you can find in your community and one use of water.

criteria.description: Names a correct source (e.g., river, tap)
Names a correct use (e.g., drinking, washing)

hints: What do you use it for?
questions.explanation: A river is a source, and drinking is a use.
